title: Validation and Measurement
subtitle: Evaluate both the result and the path taken to produce it
summary: Pip’s demo delivers a lovely confirmation, but no ticket refund occurs. Evaluation must examine outcomes and the route used to reach them. Pip gathers ordinary, ambiguous, adversarial, and edge cases so a persuasive answer cannot hide a wrong action.

concepts.title: Measurement goals
concepts.body: Pip’s guide politely confirms a refund that never happened. Evaluation starts with task-specific success, not merely exact-match wording. Pip separately scores authorized amount, completed transaction, quality, safety, latency, and cost. Fluency cannot earn completion credit for an unsuccessful action.

concepts.title: Trajectory metrics
concepts.body: Pip gets the right arrival time after seven paid lookups. The final answer hides waste. A trajectory includes decisions, tool calls, observations, and outcome, exposing wrong tools, loops, and unsupported steps. Pip reviews the path as well as the destination.

concepts.title: Evaluation sets
concepts.body: Pip’s test set begins with easy refunds. Reviewers add ambiguous ticket references, canceled bookings, adversarial requests, and edge cases. Model-generated cases expand coverage only when humans check and refine expected behavior. Pip keeps the living set a trustworthy specification.

concepts.title: Lifecycle integration
concepts.body: Pip fixes a production cancellation failure. The case joins the baseline and regression suite before the next orchestration release. Development and promotion checks compare changes and targeted new cases. Pip tests general improvement rather than retiring evaluation after a good demo.

misconceptions.claim: Measurement goals is provided automatically by a more capable model.
misconceptions.correction: Evaluation starts with explicit metrics tied to the task. For language agents, exact-match answers often fail to capture usefulness, so teams measure quality, safety, cost, latency, and successful completion.

misconceptions.claim: Trajectory metrics removes the need for evaluation or human judgment.
misconceptions.correction: A trajectory includes model decisions, tool calls, observations, and final outcome. Inspecting the path can reveal a wrong tool, unnecessary loop, or unsupported step hidden by a plausible final answer. Evaluation and appropriate oversight remain necessary.

scenario.title: Support evaluation launch
scenario.context: A new agent has a strong demo but little coverage for cancellations and ambiguous requests.

options.label: Build a reviewed living evaluation set before rollout
options.benefit: Defines expected behavior and catches edge cases.
options.cost: Launch is delayed while cases are curated.
options.consequence: A cancellation case exposes an unsafe tool path before users see it.

options.label: Ship and use complaints as evaluation
options.cost: Users bear discovery costs and feedback is uneven.
options.consequence: The team cannot tell whether a later change improved quality.

scenario.debrief: Both choices can fit different constraints. The decision should state stakes, reversibility, evidence, and who owns correction.

quiz.question: An agent reaches a correct answer after an unauthorized action. How should it be evaluated?
options: The trajectory fails an important constraint despite its final answer.
It is fully successful because the answer is correct.
Only the response length needs to be checked.
quiz.explanation: Evaluation must examine actions and constraints, not only terminal text.

quiz.question: Why include edge cases in an evaluation set?
options: They guarantee coverage of every possible production input.
They expose failures that average-case examples can hide.
They make representative ordinary cases unnecessary.
quiz.explanation: A useful set includes expected work and consequential failure modes while acknowledging incomplete coverage.

quiz.question: What should happen when a production failure is understood?
options: Remove similar cases from evaluation to restore the score.
Change the metric without investigating the behavior.
Add a relevant regression case and rerun it for future changes.
quiz.explanation: A failure becomes useful feedback when it can prevent the same defect from silently returning.
